tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move to the list, check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that moving it onto the destination peg does not place a larger disk on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you generate a move, verify the move respects the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, or moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints; use it to temporarily hold a peg clear for moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to free a peg that contains larger disks, move the smallest disk onto another peg first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 2 onto a peg that still has disk 1 on top, instead of moving disk 1 elsewhere first.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the target configuration already has correctly placed larger disks, avoid moving them.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 off a peg that already holds the correctly ordered stack [5,4] when the goal is to keep them.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg after the larger ones are already in place.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final configuration, start with the biggest disk and work downwards.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 3 onto the goal peg before moving disk 5, causing later re‑ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, ensure the last syntactically correct list in the response is the move list, so the verifier can parse it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of your answer, output the move list as the final parseable structure.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure source and destination pegs are clear of smaller disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, make sure its source peg has no smaller disks on top and the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you plan to move a disk that is not the smallest.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 from a peg where disk 1 is on top, or moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the answer within token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the move list becomes long, consider using the minimal number of moves for the sub‑problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Generating an excessively long move list that gets truncated by the token limit.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, mentally simulate each move on the initial configuration to ensure the final configuration exactly matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before finalizing the answer, double‑check the end state.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Outputting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the destination; this pattern solves arbitrary sub‑towers within the overall problem.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous stack of disks (e.g., clearing the target peg or rebuilding a sub‑tower) as part of the overall solution.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a three‑disk stack directly without first moving the top two disks to the auxiliary peg, leading to illegal moves.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model focuses on reasoning text and forgets to include the required move list at the end.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After completing the reasoning, explicitly write the move list as the final parseable list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a move based on goal proximity without checking size constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may pick a disk that is buried under smaller disks, ignoring the top‑only rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg before moving it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated answer exceeds the token limit, causing the final part of the move list to be cut off.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move sequence concise, using optimal or near‑optimal solutions, and place the move list at the very end.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of disk locations during multi‑step reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an explicit mental (or written) representation of each peg's contents after every move.
